title: The balanced-partition conjecture for the $\mathsf a;q$-down-degree expectation
source: Jang Soo Kim, Michael J. Schlosser and Meesue Yoo, “Enumeration of standard barely set-valued tableaux of shifted shapes”, arXiv:2006.03253 (2020); Electron. J. Combin. (2023), Conjecture A.2. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.03253)

lanes.final_paper_definition_and_prior_art_che: final-paper-check-340107-346782-372803-opus-20261119-r1/CHECK-346782.md, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; revised paper used (Claude Opus 5.5)

significance.root_decision: For every nonempty balanced partition (in the journal's sense: the upper left corner of each addable cell lies on the diagonal line), the a;q-weighted expectation of the down-degree statistic of Kim, Schlosser and Yoo equals the conjectured quotient of a;q-numbers, as an identity in the field of rational functions Q(a,q); the denominator is proved nonzero. This is Conjecture A.2. The proof is a telescoping corner identity. The formula fails for every unbalanced shape tested, so the hypothesis is needed.
significance.caveat: 'Balanced' is read as in the journal version (upper left corner of each addable cell on the line); the arXiv wording is ambiguous. Bounded literature search only; Hopkins, Lazar and Linusson remark in print that they could not connect the conjecture to their methods.

root_basis: Root extracted the three modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, axioms exactly the allowed three, no forbidden tokens), and screened the Principia archive (300 ids), the omega registry and GitHub by id. An independent Opus referee compared the Lean definitions word by word with the arXiv and journal texts and the MathDB record, verified the result with its own scripts, read the paper line by line and refreshed the prior-art search.
